clue.text: Gradgrind's final answer: 'Much obliged for facts!'

indicators.note: the final letter of the name Gradgrind is the one taken

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you, a way of saying much obliged

explanation.surface: Dickens's fact-obsessed schoolmaster Gradgrind signs off grateful for yet more facts.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Gradgrind, in Dickens's Hard Times, cares only for facts, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are pieces of information, the plain facts and figures used for reasoning.

clue.text: Free dentistry not unknown to be harsh

indicators.note: free here means released from its order, so the letters are loosened and rearranged
not tells us to leave out the following item from the letters

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: Someone protests loudly that dental treatment ought to be free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not unknown' removes Y from DENTISTRY, and 'Free' shuffles the remaining DENTISTR.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or sound is loud, grating and harsh on the ear.

clue.text: Place a trap in the earth?

parts.note: PL is the usual abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
a net is a device for trapping fish or animals

explanation.surface: Instructions for setting a snare by digging it into the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth' looks like soil to dig into; with 'the' and the question mark it is our world, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one of the bodies orbiting the Sun, an example signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Great game for a litter lout!

definitions.text: Great game for a litter lout!

parts.words: Great game for a litter lout!
parts.note: a litter lout drops waste paper, so a game of chasing paper round would suit one

explanation.walkthrough: A paperchase is a cross-country race following a trail of scattered paper, so it literally involves strewing litter.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is a hare-and-hounds run following a trail of torn paper laid by the leaders.

clue.text: Spectacular springs, beyond question — autumn pales, sadly

indicators.note: beyond says the following letters come after the first piece
sadly signals the words autumn pales are taken in a wretched, disordered state and rearranged

explanation.surface: A melancholy observation that autumn fades, while spring is beyond doubt spectacular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges AUTUMN PALES into UANTUMLEAPS, placed after Q. 'Spectacular springs' suggests the season; it means great jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatic sudden advances are called by this physics-derived phrase, i.e. huge jumps forward.

clue.text: Measure starting points for qualification using athletes' reaction times

indicators.note: the starting points are the initial letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Sprinters qualify for a race according to how quickly they react to the starting gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A quart is a unit of liquid volume, two pints, so it is a measure.

clue.text: Broadcasting after pain, one gets into muddle — like Ivana Trump perhaps?

indicators.note: gets into says the run of pieces goes inside the word for muddle

parts.note: a mess is a muddle

indicators.note: after places the broadcasting piece behind the pain and one pieces

parts.note: ill can mean harm or trouble, a pain
I is the Roman numeral for one
on air means being broadcast

explanation.surface: A broadcaster in pain gets into a mess, with a nod to Trump's ex-wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets into' puts the run inside the muddle word. Ivana Trump, Donald Trump's first wife, was a wealthy businesswoman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich woman worth millions is an example, as the question mark shows, of the kind of wealthy figure Ivana Trump was.

clue.text: See 5
Alcohol's an insufficient slant on prison uprising

definitions.note: read as alcohol is; the plural answer is spirits as a class of drink

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece
insufficient says the word falls short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a spin is a slant or bias put on a story

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A complaint that drink is given too little attention in reports of a jail riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insufficient' cuts SPIN to SPI; 'uprising' turns STIR to RITS beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are distilled alcoholic drinks such as gin and whisky.

clue.text: Claim a last (piece of) round sausage

indicators.note: turned round means the letters run backwards
a piece of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a claim to the final slice of a round sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters IMALAS sit inside 'Claim a last'; 'round' turns them back.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced Italian sausage usually eaten sliced.

clue.text: Hang around outskirts of Ilfracombe in frillies

parts.note: to linger is to hang around

indicators.note: the outskirts are the outermost letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: Someone loiters on the edge of a Devon seaside town dressed in frilly underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilfracombe is a seaside resort in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Frillies is informal for women's frilly underwear, the same garments as lingerie.

clue.text: Stumped, judge gains point in 'Mastermind'

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
to rate is to judge or assess
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant on the BBC's Mastermind is stumped but the judge awards a point.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running British TV quiz; here the word means a planner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastermind plans a scheme cleverly, just as a strategist devises plans and tactics.

clue.text: Happy with Carol, creatively made-up?

indicators.note: creatively suggests the letters are worked into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A cheerful carol is creatively composed, perhaps on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocryphal story is of doubtful truth, probably invented or fictitious.

clue.text: Cutting blow

definitions.meaning: a short piece of film or newspaper cut out is a ...
a ... round the ear is a smack or blow

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an extract snipped from film or print and a sharp smack.

clue.text: Filming Monroe and Ekberg, perhaps? Heavenly bodies!

definitions.meaning: making a film of famous actresses such as Marilyn Monroe and Anita Ekberg is photographing film stars
meteors streaking across the night sky

explanation.walkthrough: Marilyn Monroe and Anita Ekberg were film stars famed for their figures, hence 'heavenly bodies' too.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteors seen as bright streaks are popularly called this; also the act of filming movie stars.

clue.text: Strand's northward buttress

parts.note: a strand is a shore or beach; the 's simply links
in a down clue northward means upwards, so up

explanation.surface: A road called the Strand runs north to a supporting wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, but here it means a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop something up with supports is to strengthen it as a buttress does.

clue.text: In classy bar I tempted bon vivant

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A smart bar tempted a pleasure-loving gourmet inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to luxury and the good life is a lover of fine living, a bon vivant.

clue.text: Swivel in space and dock

indicators.note: to swivel is to turn round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: A boat turns in open water and then comes alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to tie it up at a berth, which is to dock it.

clue.text: The bumf I'll spread's a minuscule amount

indicators.note: spread is spread out, scattering the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Paperwork spreads about, but turns out to be only a tiny quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: As much as a sewing thimble holds is a tiny quantity, a very small amount of liquid.

clue.text: Mock priest's last service

parts.note: to tease is to mock

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone ridicules a clergyman's final church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests worship; it is a set of china.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea service is the matching cups, saucers and pot used to serve the drink.

clue.text: Exercising university chorus

parts.note: to chorus is to sing together

explanation.surface: A university choir rehearses its singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising a right or skill means employing it, putting it to use.

clue.text: Souvenir from 'Tower Tipple'

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
sake is Japanese rice wine, a tipple

explanation.surface: A gift-shop bottle labelled Tower Tipple, brought home as a reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento kept in memory of a person or place is a souvenir.

clue.text: Growing endless fruit

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: raising crops is growing them

explanation.surface: Fruit that keeps growing without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a familiar kind of dried fruit.

clue.text: Birdies with red parts out of sight could be these?

definitions.text: Birdies with red parts out of sight could be these?

indicators.note: the letters of red are parted from the other word and vanish
could be says the remaining letters may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Golfers' birdies, or little birds whose red markings are hidden, could be these.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R, E, D out of BIRDIES and rearrange the B, I, I, S left. The whole clue then describes the birds too.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-billed wading birds, often white without any red, might fairly be called birdies.

clue.text: Act thus for testing eating irons, etc?

parts.note: taken as an instruction, placing the letters of ... in a new order gives testing

explanation.surface: Instructions for how to proceed when trying something out.
explanation.walkthrough: Eating irons is slang for cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: The knives, forks and spoons laid for one diner at table make up one diner's set of cutlery.
